output:
I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data.

I wrote `/app/bin/payroll.py` and ran it on `/app/data`, saving the result as `/app/out/payroll.json`. `python3 /app/tools/check_payroll.py` reports that every value matches the approved figures. That covers all 150 employees on each of the five fields, the four exception counts and the totals. I didn't test it on any other period's exports.

The script uses only the standard library. It reads all seven export formats, including gzip files detected by their first bytes, and applies the corrections and the rules in `payroll-rules.md`. Repeated local times in the fall-back hour are resolved by each format's own rule. It does not hard-code anything specific to this period.

For this period the script reports 4,430 shifts and a total gross of 1,138,755.89. It counts 131 open shifts, 78 orphan outs, 278 duplicates dropped and 279 corrections applied.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -100; cat docs/*.md

cd /app; sed -n 50,200p docs/exports.md; echo ======; cat docs/output.md | head -60; ls data data/exports data/corrections; ls data/exports/*|wc -l; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -80; head -c 600 tools/reference-digests.json

cd /app/data; cat period.json sites.csv; head -5 employees.csv rates.csv; wc -l employees.csv rates.csv; head -5 corrections/batch-1.csv; for s in exports/*; do echo "== $s"; ls $s | head -3; ls $s | wc -l; done; file exports/*/* | awk -F: '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c

cd /app/data/exports; python3 - <<'E'
import glob,gzip,os
for s in sorted(os.listdir('.')):
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(s+'/*'))
    gz=[f for f in fs if open(f,'rb').read(2)==b'\x1f\x8b']
    print('==',s,len(fs),'gz',len(gz))
    f=fs[10]
    b=open(f,'rb').read()
    if b[:2]==b'\x1f\x8b': b=gzip.decompress(b)
    print(f); print(b[:500].decode())
E

cd /app/data; cat corrections/*.csv | cut -d, -f3 | sort | uniq -c; grep -h -v '^C' corrections/*.csv | head; grep -c . corrections/*.csv | head -3; sort -t, -k2 rates.csv | head -3; awk -F, '{print $1}' rates.csv | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3

python3 -V; python3 -c "import zoneinfo;print(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('Asia/Kathmandu'))"; cd /app/data; sort -u rates.csv | awk -F, 'NR>1{print $1}' | sort | uniq -d | head -3; python3 - <<'E'
import csv
r=list(csv.DictReader(open('rates.csv')))
emps={x['employee_id'] for x in csv.DictReader(open('employees.csv'))}
have={x['employee_id'] for x in r}
print(len(emps-have), len(have-emps))
from collections import defaultdict
d=defaultdict(list)
for x in r:d[x['employee_id']].append(x['effective_from'])
print([ (e,min(v)) for e,v in d.items() if e in emps and min(v)>'2026-09-28'])
print([(k,v) for k,v in d.items() if len(v)!=len(set(v))])
E

cd /app; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('out/payroll.json'));print(d['exceptions'],d['totals'])"

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py (stdlib only, implements all documented formats and rules) and saved /app/out/payroll.json; tools/check_payroll.py reports every value matching the approved figures."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
